question: Which memory-wiki isolation contract should OpenClaw support for shared-gateway multi-agent setups: plugin-owned per-agent vault routing, generic agents.list[].plugins config overrides, context-aware vault.path templating, or documented unsupported shared-gateway isolation?
rationale: The choice controls sensitive memory visibility, config precedence, plugin SDK surface, CLI/gateway semantics, and upgrade expectations, so automation cannot safely select the permanent product/security boundary from source evidence alone.

options.title: Design plugin-owned vault isolation
options.body: Add a memory-wiki-owned per-agent or context-aware vault contract first, coordinated with the broader per-agent plugin config issue but not blocked on it.

options.title: Wait for generic plugin overrides
options.body: Keep this issue open behind #55401 and solve memory-wiki through a shared agents.list[].plugins precedence, SecretRef, validation, and lifecycle contract.

options.title: Document unsupported shared-gateway isolation
options.body: Leave memory-wiki global for now and document separate gateways or separate installs as the only supported hard isolation boundary.

recommendation.title: Design plugin-owned vault isolation
recommendation.body: Add a memory-wiki-owned per-agent or context-aware vault contract first, coordinated with the broader per-agent plugin config issue but not blocked on it.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans plugin config runtime, memory-wiki doctor/upgrade behavior, and security-sensitive memory isolation where this owner has the strongest recent boundary history.
